titulo: Estar + gerund, ir a + infinitive and acabar de: Combining the three in context

aula.titulo: Estar + gerund, ir a + infinitive and acabar de
aula.objetivo: Talk about what's happening right now with «estar» + gerund, about the near future with «ir a» + infinitive, and about the recent past with «acabar de» + infinitive, form the regular and irregular gerund, and place the pronouns correctly.

blocos.titulo: Choosing the structure and watching out for false friends
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to choose, think about the timing of the action: right now → «estar + gerundio»; right after → «ir a + infinitivo»; right before → «acabar de + infinitivo». STEP 2: with «todavía» (still) and «ya» (already), the gerund shows an action in progress: «Todavía estoy trabajando», «Ya estoy llegando». STEP 3: to say what isn't happening, put «no» before «estar»: «No estoy trabajando». STEP 4: in questions, the gerund comes after the verb: «¿Qué estás haciendo?», «¿Dónde estáis comiendo?» STEP 5: false friends in this lesson: «cena» isn't a movie scene; it's dinner. «Cenar» means to have dinner. A movie scene is «escena» — close enough to the English word "scene" that it's easy to mix up with «cena» in the other direction too. STEP 6: «embarazada» means pregnant, not embarrassed — this is one of the best-known traps for an English speaker, since the word looks almost exactly like "embarrassed." For embarrassed, use «avergonzada». STEP 7: «constipado» means to have a cold, not constipated in the digestive sense — another word that looks like it should mean something else. STEP 8: «pasarlo bien» means to have a good time: «¡Que lo paséis bien!» (Spain) or «¡Que lo pases bien!». STEP 9: on the phone, the most common question is «¿Qué estás haciendo?» or «¿Qué haces?», and answering with the gerund feels completely natural.
blocos.comparacao: English speakers run into «embarazada» as practically a trap built for them: it's one of the most famous false friends in Spanish precisely because it looks so close to "embarrassed" while meaning pregnant. «Cena» has the same kind of near-miss with "scene," even though the real word for a movie scene, «escena», is the one that actually resembles it.

tabela.exemplo: [misto] La cena es a las nueve.
[misto] La última escena es muy triste.

erros.errado: [misto] Vamos a ver una cena de la película.
erros.certo: [misto] Vamos a ver una escena de la película.
erros.motivo: «Cena» means dinner; a movie scene is «escena».
For the near future, use «ir a», not the gerund of «ir».
After «estar», the verb goes in the gerund.

blocos.contexto: Ana calls Pablo and they tell each other what they're doing and what they're going to do.

linhas.pt: — Hi, Pablo. What are you doing?

linhas.ru: — Estoy cocinando. Acabo de llegar a casa.
linhas.pt: — I'm cooking. I just got home.
linhas.audio: Estoy cocinando. Acabo de llegar a casa.

linhas.ru: — Todavía no. Voy a cenar dentro de media hora. ¿Y tú?
linhas.pt: — Not yet. I'm going to have dinner in half an hour. And you?
linhas.audio: Todavía no. Voy a cenar dentro de media hora. ¿Y tú?

linhas.ru: — Estoy esperando el autobús. Voy a ir al cine con Marta.
linhas.pt: — I'm waiting for the bus. I'm going to the movies with Marta.
linhas.audio: Estoy esperando el autobús. Voy a ir al cine con Marta.

linhas.pt: — What movie are you two going to see?

linhas.ru: — Aún no lo sabemos. Estamos mirando la cartelera en el móvil.
linhas.pt: — We don't know yet. We're looking at the listings on my phone.
linhas.audio: Aún no lo sabemos. Estamos mirando la cartelera en el móvil.

linhas.pt: — Are you two going to have dinner afterward?

linhas.ru: — Sí, vamos a cenar en un bar cerca del cine.
linhas.pt: — Yes, we're going to have dinner at a bar near the theater.
linhas.audio: Sí, vamos a cenar en un bar cerca del cine.

blocos.enunciado: Imagine a phone call with a friend: ask what they're doing, say what you're doing, and agree on what each of you is going to do. Speak out loud, using all three structures.
Say one sentence with each structure: «estar» + gerund, «ir a» + infinitive, and «acabar de» + infinitive.
